alternate_names: Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Lling Monastery (Upper section)

history.period: Founded 1965-1966; main prayer hall added later by the 13th reincarnate
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery of the Gelugpa (Yellow Hat) tradition. The Upper Gompa is the main and most-visited of three sections (Upper, Middle, Lower) of the GRL (Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Lling) Monastery at Bomdila. Founded in 1965-66 by the 12th reincarnate of Tsona Gontse Rinpoche as a replica of the Tsona Gontse Monastery in South Tibet; the main prayer hall was added later by the 13th reincarnate. Set at ~8,500 ft atop a hill with panoramic views of Bomdila town, it houses a large prayer hall, a Buddha temple, a school for young monks, residential quarters, and a large prayer wheel. RELATED ROW: CSV seq 69 (Middle Gompa) is the middle section of the SAME monastery complex — filed separately per instructions.

name: Upper Gompa (Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Lling Monastery)
town_description: Bomdila (elev. ~7,300-8,000 ft) is the headquarters of West Kameng district, a scenic hill town on the Tezpur-Bhalukpong-Tawang route, known for its Buddhist monasteries, panoramic views of the Kangto and Gorichen peaks, and as the main stopover between the plains of Assam and Tawang.

travel.airport: Tezpur airport is the nearest (~175 km, verify); Guwahati (Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International) is the main gateway (~330 km).
travel.railway: Nearest railheads: Bhalukpong / Tezpur / Guwahati (verify); official West Kameng tourism lists Bhalukpong, Tezpur and Guwahati.
travel.road: On the Tezpur-Bhalukpong-Bomdila-Tawang highway (NH-13); Upper Gompa is a short drive/trek above Bomdila town on the hilltop.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April - pleasant weather, clear views (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented reliably; most Arunachal gompas admit daytime visitors, with morning and evening prayers (verify). Dress respectfully; photography may be restricted inside prayer halls.
